question: Can conditional mapping uncertainty choose useful independent identities to measure under process mismatch?
outcome: Across 48 new systems, entropy selection reduces mean measurements to exact recovery. In changed administrative systems, it also increases wrong decisions from a 95%-mass stopping diagnostic: at 35% change, 2.500 versus 3.552 measurements but 25/96 versus 17/96 stopping errors against random selection. All 576 conditions and 15,552 prefix records are retained.
challenge: Measurement efficiency and a calibrated stopping decision are distinct targets. Two pilots failed on NumPy Boolean serialization. Fixed-score restriction makes first-correct recovery monotone, rendering one planned diagnostic redundant.
remedy: Separate query/response oracle interfaces, exhaustive compatible bijections, saved complete histories, paired system-level comparisons, startup serialization checks and independent reindexed likelihood/policy replay.
retry_when: A physically specified measurement likelihood/cost, generative-model disagreement, verification design or separately declared stopping-calibration procedure changes the acquisition problem.
